which are synthesized from arachidonic acid, modulate the 
inﬂ ammatory response resulting in tissue edema, mucus secre-
tion, smooth-muscle proliferation, and powerful bronchocon-
striction. Two types of leukotriene-based medications have 
been developed to combat asthma: leukotriene inhibitors that
interfere with the actual synthesis of leukotrienes (Zyﬂ o™), and 
leukotriene antagonists that block their action at the receptor 
level (Accolate™ and Singulair™).
One possible approach to preventing the synthesis of leu-
kotrienes is through dietary modiﬁ cation. Normally, human 
inﬂ ammatory cells contain high amounts of the omega-6 fatty 
acid, arachidonic acid, and low amounts of omega-3 fatty 
acids.31, 32 Because both omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids are 
metabolized by a common pathway, an excess of omega-3
fatty acids interferes with the metabolism of the omega-6 
fatty acids and reduces their incorporation into tissue lipids.
